candidate.answerReason: The sides form a right triangle of area 120 square inches. Splitting it into three triangles with height equal to the inradius gives 120=30r, hence r=4.

methods.label: Method 1: Split the triangle into three areas
methods.explanation:
The side lengths suggest checking for a right triangle:
\[
10^2+24^2=100+576=676=26^2.
\]
By the converse of the Pythagorean theorem, the right angle is at \(C\). Thus the area of \(ABC\) is
\[
K=\frac12(10)(24)=120\text{ square inches}.
\]
Let \(I\) be the center of the inscribed circle and let its radius be \(r\). Join \(I\) to the three vertices. This splits \(ABC\) into three triangles whose bases are the original sides. Each has height \(r\), because a radius to a point of tangency is perpendicular to the side. Adding their areas gives
\[
120=\frac12(24r+10r+26r)=30r.
\]
Therefore \(r=4\) inches, choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses elementary right-triangle recognition and derives the area-inradius relation by adding triangle areas.

methods.label: Method 2: Use equal tangent lengths
methods.explanation:
Since \(10^2+24^2=26^2\), the converse of the Pythagorean theorem shows that \(AC\perp BC\).

Let the inscribed circle have center \(I\), radius \(r\), and points of tangency \(P\) on \(AC\), \(Q\) on \(BC\), and \(T\) on \(AB\). The radii \(IP\) and \(IQ\) are perpendicular to their tangent sides. Consequently \(CPIQ\) has four right angles and two adjacent sides \(IP=IQ=r\), so it is a square. Hence \(CP=CQ=r\).

The remaining portions of the legs are
\[
AP=24-r,\qquad BQ=10-r.
\]
Tangent segments from the same outside point are equal, so \(AT=AP\) and \(BT=BQ\). Adding these segments along \(AB\) gives
\[
26=AT+BT=(24-r)+(10-r).
\]
Thus \(2r=8\), so the radius is \(4\) inches, choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses right angles, square properties, and equal tangent segments, with a simple linear equation.

candidate.annotationRationale: Finding an incircle radius is the route-neutral target. Both methods recognize the right triangle and use perpendicular tangent radii. The first method uses triangle areas and only the K=rs portion of the area-radius node. The second uses equal tangent lengths and a square; those are alternative method components.
